ASPI.summary: ASPI rose 20.6% today to $2.08 while SPY was up only 0.3%, so the move is stock-specific. The news flow (Nov 6, Yahoo) reports partner Tetra4, a Renergen subsidiary, completed commissioning and began stable liquid helium production at South Africa's Virginia Gas Project, with initial deliveries starting. The stock is still down about 27% over one month and only up 2.7% over five days, so today's gain partly recovers a sharp prior pullback.

OUST.summary: OUST rose 14.0% today to $34.79 while SPY was up only 0.31%, so the move is stock-specific. Fundamentals are supportive: Q3 2026 revenue was a record $59.3M (up 50% YoY), Q4 guidance is $61-64M, cash is over $400M, and Amerx upgraded the stock to Buy on Nov 4 (price target lowered to $52.5). The stock gave back gains on Nov 5, and a 14-day news search finds no catalyst for today's rebound, so the cause is unconfirmed. The stock is still down 16.5% over one month, though up 17% over five days.

LAES.summary: LAES (SEALSQ) rose 7.3% today to $1.32 while SPY was up only 0.3%, so the move is stock-specific. The 14-day news flow shows only routine items (a post-quantum partnership with TechAgency, a wave-energy MoU, and a Cannes event), and no earnings are scheduled in the next 45 days, so nothing clearly explains the jump. The stock is still down 10.2% over 5 days and 43.6% over one month, so this looks like a bounce after a steep sell-off rather than a change in fundamentals.

TGEN.summary: TGEN (Tecogen) rose 12.4% today to $1.72 while SPY gained 0.3%, so the move is stock-specific. No news in the past 14 days explains the bounce; the only items are the Nov 4 notice of the Q3 2026 earnings release and an unrelated Fortune Brands result. The stock is still down 13.6% over 5 days and 37.7% over one month, so today's gain looks like a partial rebound from a steep decline, not a fundamental reversal. Q3 results are scheduled for Nov 12 (5 days out) with EPS estimate of -$0.065 and revenue estimate of about $6.54M.

ETH-USD.summary: ETH-USD closed at $2,241.92, up 0.31% today, in line with SPY (+0.31%), so there was no stock-specific move. Over one month ETH is down 12.9% versus SPY's -5.4%, a meaningful underperformance, though over five days it is roughly flat (-0.3%) against SPY's -2.7%. Recent news is mixed: US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs saw $530M in combined outflows on Nov 6, and Ethereum developers paused a Glamsterdam testnet fork over smart contract risks; offsetting this, Russia finalized retail crypto trading rules (ETH included) ahead of a Nov 17 rollout, and Amundi tokenized an equity index fund on Ethereum.

MSFT.summary: MSFT closed at $530.61, down 0.99% today while SPY rose 0.31%, so the stock underperformed the market by about 1.3 points on a move well below the 5% threshold. It is up 1.67% over five days versus SPY's -2.7%, and roughly flat over one month (+0.16%) versus SPY's -5.39%, so it has held up better than the broad market. No earnings are scheduled in the next 45 days, and no stock-specific news was pulled because the move was small.
